This is a review of a task, not the task itself. Do not do the clinical work. You have only read tools: there is no write tool and no finish tool.

Below is the instruction an agent receives for task crc-care-gap. Read it, then use the read tools to read everything it depends on: the clinic policies it names or that govern it (read_policy), the patients, orders, results, notes and inbox items it points at, and your own context (get_context).

Report every ambiguity you find, where a careful clinician could not tell what the task wants:
- two_readings: a sentence of the instruction or a policy reads two ways, and the two readings lead to different actions;
- missing_fact: a fact the work needs (a date, a dose, a threshold, a recipient, a patient) is not in the instruction, the policies or the chart;
- conflict: two sources (the instruction, a policy, a note, an order, a result) say different things about the same point.

Quote the exact words each finding rests on. Leave out what is only hard, long or clinically unusual but has one reading. If you find none, say so with an empty list.

End with one final message that holds only this JSON object, with no text before or after it:
{"findings": [{"kind": "two_readings" | "missing_fact" | "conflict", "source": "<instruction, or the policy id, or the resource as Type/id>", "quote": "<the exact words>", "readings": ["<what one reading asks the agent to do>", "<what another asks>"], "explanation": "<why a careful clinician could not tell which is meant>"}]}
Give readings two or more entries for two_readings and conflict, and none for missing_fact.

The instruction for crc-care-gap:

<instruction>
Please run CRC outreach for my panel group 'Okafor CRC 2026' per RBC-QM-02.

Finish with a table listing every patient, their status and the reason.

— Dr. Okafor

</instruction>

content.text:
RBC-QM-02 Colorectal cancer screening outreach, 2026

Applies to colorectal cancer screening outreach for a clinician's panel group.
Adapted from CMS130v14, Colorectal Cancer Screening, 2026 performance period. The panel group takes the place of the measure's visit requirement.

§1 Measurement period
The measurement period is calendar year 2026. Years in §3 and §4 are calendar years.

§2 Population
Panel members aged 46 to 75 years at the end of the measurement period.

§3 Screening
A patient's screening is up to date with any one of:
- a fecal occult blood test (FOBT, guaiac or immunochemical/FIT) during the measurement period;
- a stool DNA with FIT test (sDNA-FIT) during the measurement period or the 2 years before it;
- a flexible sigmoidoscopy or a CT colonography during the measurement period or the 4 years before it;
- a colonoscopy during the measurement period or the 9 years before it.

§4 Exclusions
A patient is excluded who has any of:
- colorectal cancer or a total colectomy, at any time;
- hospice care or palliative care during any part of the measurement period;
- age 66 or older at the end of the measurement period and living long term in a nursing home;
- age 66 or older at the end of the measurement period, frailty (an active diagnosis) at any point during the measurement period, and advanced illness: an advanced illness diagnosis during the measurement period or the year before it, or a dementia medication during the measurement period or the year before it.

§5 Outreach
A patient in the population who is not excluded and whose screening is not up to date has an open gap.
For each open gap, order a FIT kit (a ServiceRequest) and send the patient an outreach message.
Do not place a FIT order for a patient who already has an active FIT order.

§6 Report
Give every panel member one status (screening up to date, open gap, excluded, or not in the population) and the reason for it.

Tolu Adeyemi, MD
